title: Inference for stochastic differential equations driven by weighted sub-fractional Brownian motion using neural networks and the Euler approximation
summary:
arXiv:2610.00793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the estimation of drift, diffusion, and noise covariance from discrete observations of stochastic differential equations driven by Gaussian processes. For a fixed observation horizon $T>0$ and a known initial state $x_0\in\mathbb R$, we study  egin{equation*} dX_t=a(X_t)\,dt+\sigma(X_t)\,dZ_t^{ eta,f}, \qquad X_0=x_0,\quad 0\leq t\leq T. \end{equation*} \smallskip
oindent Here $a:\mathbb R	o\mathbb R$ is the drift coefficient, $\sigma:\mathbb R	o(0,\infty)$ is the diffusion coefficient, and $Z^{ eta,f}$ is a centered Gaussian process from the weighted sub-fractional Brownian family, with covariance  egin{equation*} \operatorname{Cov}(Z_s^{ eta,f},Z_t^{ eta,f}) =\int_0^{s\wedge t} f(r)q_ eta(s-r,t-r)\,dr, \qquad 0\leq s,t\leq T. \end{equation*} \smallskip
oindent Here $s\wedge t=\min\{s,t\}$. The temporal weight $f:[0,T]	o[0,\infty)$ is measurable, bounded, and positive almost everywhere, and $ eta\in(0,2)$ is the covariance exponent. For $u,v\geq0$, the kernel is $q_ eta(u,v)=[u^ eta+v^ eta-(u+v)^ eta]/(1- eta)$ when $ eta
e1$. Its continuous extension at $ eta=1$ is $q_1(u,v)=(u+v)\log(u+v)-u\log u-v\log v$, with $0\log0=0$. Using the Euler approximation, we reconstruct the Gaussian driving increments from observed transitions and use their joint density to obtain a trajectory likelihood. Neural and radial-basis representations model the drift, diffusion, and normalized temporal weight, while a likelihood profile estimates the covariance exponent and diffusion scale. We compare the method with two neural alternatives on the same simulated trajectories in twenty coefficient settings.
